description_long: The supplied TrumpFile summary says the Treasury Department canceled 31 Booz Allen Hamilton contracts worth $21 million on January 26, 2026, citing an IRS data leak from more than five years earlier. It says Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accused Booz Allen of failing to protect sensitive taxpayer information, while the company responded that the employee used government systems and that it did not store taxpayer data on its own systems. title: White House Pressed Pentagon to Expedite $620 Million Loan to Trump Jr.-Linked Vulcan Elements
description_short: ProPublica reported that a White House request helped fast-track a $620 million Pentagon loan to Vulcan Elements, where Trump Jr.’s venture firm held a stake.
description_medium: ProPublica reported that Donald Trump Jr.’s venture-capital firm took an undisclosed stake in Vulcan Elements about three months before the Pentagon announced plans for a $620 million loan to the critical-minerals startup. Defense Department records and interviews tied the request to White House adviser Peter Navarro. Pentagon and company representatives denied Trump Jr.’s involvement or political favoritism.
description_long: ProPublica reported that the Pentagon planned a $620 million loan for Vulcan Elements, a critical-minerals startup, about three months after a venture-capital firm associated with Donald Trump Jr. took an undisclosed stake in the company. Interviews and Defense Department records reviewed by ProPublica indicated that White House adviser Peter Navarro, a friend of Trump Jr., initiated the request. A Pentagon official said Vulcan was the only deal among dozens under consideration started by a top presidential aide. Another person involved in the process said staff were told to move unusually quickly, working late nights to complete the loan in weeks. Trump Jr.’s spokesperson, the Pentagon, and Vulcan’s founder denied that Trump Jr. played a role or that the company received political favoritism. ProPublica described the loan as the first federal-agency deal it had directly linked to White House intervention. The reporting documents a family-linked financial stake and unusual executive involvement; it does not by itself establish unlawful conduct. The separate Public Citizen claims in the earlier draft are not supported by this linked article and have been removed.
notes: The focused ProPublica read resolves the linked-source mismatch: it reports the Vulcan Elements Pentagon loan, the undisclosed Trump Jr.-related venture stake, Navarro’s request, accelerated processing, and denials of favoritism. It does not support the separate Public Citizen account of international agreements, so that conflated framing was removed. The description reports the documented intervention and denials without presenting corruption as proven.

description_long: Trump University sold courses presented as real-estate investment instruction. The supplied litigation summary says internal sales guidance urged staff to find prospective students who were “broke” or in financial distress and encourage them to raise credit limits to pay for courses. It also says former sales manager Ronald Schnackenberg testified that he resigned because he objected to the practices, including targeting older students on fixed incomes. title: Trump signs childhood-vaccine executive order and invokes autism in remarks
description_short: Trump signs childhood-vaccine executive order and invokes autism in remarks
description_medium: On August 10, 2026, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14420 revising federal childhood-vaccine recommendations, including recommending separate administration of MMR components once available and spacing immunizations across visits. In remarks at the signing, Trump said the initiative involved autism and reiterated claims linking childhood vaccination practices to autism. Major medical and scientific reviews, including a 2025-2026 WHO evidence review, found no causal relationship between vaccines and autism.
description_long: On August 10, 2026, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14420, which revised federal childhood-vaccine recommendations and directed agencies to review and advance them as permitted by law. The order calls for separate measles, mumps, and rubella shots once those products are domestically available and, where feasible, separate visits for childhood immunizations. At the signing, Trump said the initiative involved autism and made claims about childhood vaccination practices. Those remarks are distinct from the text of the order. A World Health Organization review of evidence through 2025 concluded that the most rigorous studies do not support a causal association between vaccines and autism spectrum disorder. The sources therefore document a change in federal recommendations and the president’s autism-related rhetoric, not a scientific finding that vaccines cause autism. The executive-order date is August 10, 2026; the record’s existing start date remains August 1, 2025 and needs a separate metadata correction outside this description output.
